title: Impact of exciton-phonon and exciton-magnon interaction on transport in anisotropic 2D magnetic semiconductors
authors: Daniel Erkensten, Katarzyna Sadecka, Marie-Christin Heißenbüttel, Thorsten Deilmann, Ermin Malic
abstract: Two-dimensional magnetic semiconductors provide a unique platform for exploring the interplay between charge, lattice, spin, and light. The strong Coulomb interaction combined with long-range magnetic order enables efficient coupling between excitons and both lattice vibrations and spin excitations, thereby strongly influencing exciton dynamics and transport in these materials. Here, we develop a microscopic many-body theory of exciton--phonon and exciton--magnon interactions in mono- and bilayer CrSBr. We demonstrate that the quasi-one-dimensional character of excitons in CrSBr gives rise to strongly anisotropic exciton--phonon and exciton--magnon scattering, resulting in direction-dependent diffusion coefficients. Furthermore, we identify a distinct temperature dependence originating from one-phonon and two-magnon scattering processes, providing characteristic signatures of the underlying microscopic interactions. Our work establishes a microscopic framework for understanding exciton transport in magnetic van der Waals semiconductors and provides guidance for future optical spectroscopy and exciton transport experiments.
summary: This theoretical work develops a comprehensive many-body framework to model exciton transport in 2D magnetic semiconductors like $	ext{CrSBr}$. It quantifies how coupling to phonons and magnons causes anisotropic scattering, predicting measurable, temperature-dependent signatures in the exciton linewidths and diffusion coefficients.
main_problem: The paper investigates how exciton dynamics and transport in anisotropic 2D magnetic semiconductors are governed by the coupling to lattice vibrations (phonons) and spin excitations (magnons).
main_result: The quasi-one-dimensional nature of excitons leads to strongly anisotropic scattering, resulting in direction-dependent diffusion coefficients, and the temperature dependence of dephasing rates is characterized by distinct one-phonon and two-magnon signatures.
method: The authors developed a microscopic many-body theory, deriving coupled equations of motion for the exciton polarization using techniques like the Heisenberg equation-of-motion and applying approximations such as the Born-Markov approximation.
model_or_system: The system studied is $	ext{CrSBr}$, an anisotropic 2D magnetic semiconductor, modeled using Hamiltonians incorporating exciton, phonon, and magnon terms. The analysis covers both monolayer and bilayer (antiferromagnetic) configurations.
key_observables: Direction-dependent diffusion coefficients, exciton spectral linewidths, phonon-induced dephasing ($\gamma_{	ext{ph}}(T)$), and magnon-induced dephasing ($\gamma_{	ext{m}}(T)$).
important_parameters: Temperature ($T$), exciton binding energy ($	ext{E}_b$), and the magnon gap ($\Delta$).
main_assumptions: Approximations include the low-density limit for excitons, the use of the Born-Markov approximation, and treating the exciton-magnon interaction via one- and two-magnon terms.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the anisotropic exciton propagation, the electronic band structure, phonon dispersion, and magnon dispersion relations in $	ext{CrSBr}$.
paper_structure: The paper builds the theory by defining the Hamiltonian, deriving the equations of motion for the exciton polarization, and then calculating the dephasing rates separately for phonon and magnon interactions, distinguishing between one- and two-magnon processes.
why_interesting: The detailed derivation of temperature-dependent dephasing rates ($\propto T^2$ for magnons) and the explicit inclusion of spin-lattice coupling mechanisms provide a rich theoretical framework for understanding open quantum systems in magnetic materials.
